evals.prompt: I'm in Claude Code. Is there a skill that could help me make my React app faster? Find a few options and tell me how I'd install the best one, but don't install anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A short list of matching skills from skills.sh (found with npx skills find and a React performance query), each with name, description, publisher, and source, one recommendation with a reason, and the Claude Code install command for it. Nothing is installed.
expectations: Searches skills.sh with npx skills find and a React performance query, or says the search could not run and why
Presents each result with its name, a one-line description, who publishes it, and its source (owner/repo or skills.sh link)
Recommends one result and says why

Gives a Claude Code install command for the recommendation: npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -a claude-code, or /plugin marketplace add plus /plugin install when the repository is a plugin marketplace
Runs no install command (no npx skills add, ccpm install, or plugin install)
Does not run npx skills check or npx skills update

evals.prompt: I'm using Cowork. Find me a skill that writes README files, and install it.
evals.expected_output: Recommends Repertoire's readme-md skill as /repertoire:readme-md (or /readme-md when installed on its own). If the session already lists it, tells the user to run it. Otherwise tells the user to add the costa-marcello/repertoire marketplace in Customize > Plugins (Add > Add marketplace > Add from a repository) and install the repertoire plugin, and explains that an install inside the Cowork session would be lost when the session ends. Runs no npx skills add or ccpm install either way.
expectations: Recommends Repertoire's readme-md skill, naming it /repertoire:readme-md first and /readme-md second
Checks whether readme-md is already listed in the session; if it is, tells the user to run it instead of installing anything

When readme-md is not listed, tells the user to add the costa-marcello/repertoire marketplace through Customize > Plugins (Add > Add marketplace) and install the repertoire plugin, and explains that a skill installed inside the Cowork session would be lost when the session ends
Does not run npx skills add or ccpm install
Does not claim that it installed the skill

evals.prompt: find a skill that can fill in PDF forms. I switch between Claude Code and Cowork.
evals.expected_output: Points to Anthropic's pdf skill instead of searching for or installing a registry skill. Says it comes with Cowork and with Claude Code signed in to a claude.ai account, and gives the document-skills plugin route for Claude Code sessions that do not list it. Does not describe pdf as a Repertoire skill.
expectations: Points to Anthropic's pdf skill instead of searching the registries

Says the pdf skill comes with Cowork, and for Claude Code either confirms it is listed in the session or gives /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills plus /plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
Does not describe pdf, or any of docx, pptx, and xlsx, as a Repertoire skill
Runs no install command itself (no ccpm install, npx skills add, or plugin install)

evals.prompt: what skills do I have installed right now?
evals.expected_output: A list of the skills available in the session, taken from the skills in Claude's own context and grouped by where they come from, with a total. For Claude Code it may add what npx skills list -g and ccpm list report, and suggests /plugin for installed plugins.
expectations: Lists the skills from its own context, grouped by source (plugin, project, user, or built-in)
Reports a total count
Does not run npx skills check, which updates installed skills
Installs, removes, and updates nothing

evals.prompt: I'm in Cowork. Install the web-design-guidelines skill from vercel-labs/agent-skills so I can keep using it in later sessions.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether vercel-labs/agent-skills is a plugin marketplace (its marketplace.json returns 404, so it is not). Runs no npx skills add or ccpm install and explains why: the install would be lost with the session. Clones the repository, checks that the skill's frontmatter uses only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, and allowed-tools, zips the skill folder as web-design-guidelines, saves the ZIP to the outputs folder, and tells the user to upload it in Customize > Skills. If the clone fails, says so and offers to do the task directly or install the skill in Claude Code.
expectations: Checks for .claude-plugin/marketplace.json in vercel-labs/agent-skills, or says the check could not run
Does not run npx skills add or ccpm install, and explains that an install inside the Cowork session would be lost when the session ends
Checks the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter keys against the six an upload accepts
Saves a ZIP holding a web-design-guidelines folder with its SKILL.md to the outputs folder, or says why it could not, such as a failed clone
Tells the user to upload the ZIP in Customize > Skills and to check in a new session that the skill is listed
Does not claim that the skill is now installed
